text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000207's elevated 99215 rate falls mostly on complex patients but exceeds peers at every complexity level, and too few charts were returned to tell upcoding from a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"Most of this provider's 99215 claims are on patients with multiple chronic conditions, which fits a complex panel. But the 99215 share runs above the all-provider rate in every complexity stratum, most sharply at 4 and 5+ conditions, so patient mix alone does not fully explain the excess. The billing is also heavily weighted toward 99214, which the risk-adjusted 99215 comparison does not capture. Documentation is too thin to judge: only two 99215 charts came back, and both supported the billed level (C0097765, C0098700). The 99214 mismatch rate looks higher than peers, but it rests on just two claims (C0098108, C0098954), and the two notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed with no lab line on the claim are only weak signals. A reviewer should first request a larger chart sample focused on 99215 and 99214. Start with the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims that carry only acute or symptom codes, such as C0097919, C0098462 and C0099016, and check whether the notes show high-level medical decision making (MDM) or documented time."}
